Change 3051 patch set 1: LLM-Review +1, Verified -1. CI run 39247753239 failed only in the gating `pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.13)` cell: 16 failed, 19910 passed. All 16 are `test_live_surface_equals_golden` for the 16 hand-written MCP-only tools (none of the 48 derived tools), and each differs from the golden only in `description`. The 3.11 and 3.12 ubuntu cells ran the same test and passed; the macOS 3.13 cell runs a narrower selection that does not include it.

Root cause: Python 3.13+ strips common leading whitespace from every docstring at compile time (What's New 3.13, gh-81283). The hand-written tools' descriptions are their docstrings, so on 3.13 they advertise dedented text, while the golden was captured on 3.12 (`.github/python-version.txt`). Reproduced locally in a scratch 3.13 venv: the same 16 fail, all description-only, and all are equal after `inspect.cleandoc`. This is a property of the golden test, not of the derivation.

Fix (test only, `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_tool_surface_golden.py`, already in file_impact): the comparison stays byte-for-byte on 3.11/3.12; on 3.13+ descriptions are compared after `inspect.cleandoc`, and the docstring states why. Result: 68/68 pass on 3.12 and on 3.13, and 852 facade, secret-screen, and cross-session tests pass on 3.13. lint, typecheck, mechanism ratchet, and the ARG backlog test are green. make verify is running, then the change goes up as patch set 2.

Adjacent finding: the 48 derived tools' descriptions are string literals, not docstrings, so they carry the 3.12 indentation on every interpreter. On 3.13+, 26 of them now advertise indented continuation lines where main's 3.13 server advertised dedented text. The change is whitespace-only and the pinned 3.12 interpreter is unaffected.
